paragraphs: I am Lily, and I am ten years old. On Friday, our class goes to the bird park to see an eagle show. The bird park is near our school, so we walk. Teacher Kim gives us a paper with directions. She would like us to read it at home. Then we do not forget the way. We all wear our school clothes on the trip. I read the paper to Mia on Thursday.

Stand in a line with your friend. Go out of the school gate, and turn right. Walk along the street to the bank. The street is noisy, so stay with the line. Do not run, and do not push. The bank is a big gray building. Turn left in front of the bank. You will see a small shop on the corner. It sells cold drinks, but do not go in.

Cross the street at the crossing. Look left and right before you go. Teacher Kim goes first. Walk past a big tree. The tree is old and tall. Its shade is cool. It is a bit far, but it is not hard. You can see the park gate after five minutes. Teacher Kim has the tickets. The eagle show is at ten o'clock.

"Is the eagle really big?" asks Mia. "Yes, it is," I say. "Its wings are very long." Mia has a small bottle of water in her bag. I have my hat. Mia would like to see it fly. We say the directions again. Right at the school, left at the bank, and cross at the crossing. Now we know the way. We want Friday to come now!
